clue.text: Tuna or egg stuffed in crab cooked in beer

indicators.note: the word in puts the scrambled crab-and-egg mixture inside the drink

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

indicators.note: stuffed in means the egg goes inside the crab, like a stuffing
something cooked has been worked over, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: an egg is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A recipe: a fish dish, with egg inside crab stewed in beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a link word here; the scrambled mixture BACOR comes from 'cooked' working on the egg-stuffed crab, and 'in' wraps the beer around it.
explanation.definitionFit: The albacore is a long-finned species of tuna, often sold tinned as white tuna.

clue.text: High-yielding stock the City held

indicators.note: held means the stock-word wraps around the City's letters

parts.note: a fund is a stock or store of money
EC is the postcode of the City of London, the financial district

explanation.surface: A productive investment fund that the financial district keeps hold of.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is the City of London, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Fecund means fertile or productive, so a high-yielding crop or field is fecund.

clue.text: Assaulted, having had food in inn on journey north

indicators.note: in places the eating word inside the turned-round inn
in a down clue a journey north reads the word from bottom to top, so it is turned backwards

parts.note: a pub is an inn
having eaten is having had food

explanation.surface: Someone mugged after a meal at a pub while travelling north.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on journey north' means reading upwards, giving BUP; the eating word sits between its B and UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To be beaten up is to be violently attacked, the same as being assaulted.

clue.text: Nun, first to take wine

parts.note: a Clare is a nun of the order of Poor Clares

indicators.note: first to means only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A nun leading the way in having a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The Poor Clares are an order of Franciscan nuns, so a nun can be a Clare.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine.

clue.text: Wicked fly going around gets zapped

indicators.note: going around means the fly word wraps round the wicked word

parts.note: a ked is a wingless parasitic fly that lives on sheep
ill can mean evil or wicked, as in ill deeds

explanation.surface: An evil insect circling the room is swatted.
explanation.definitionFit: Zapped is slang for destroyed or killed, so the two past participles match.

clue.text: Actor showing energy with movement, getting to a great speed

parts.note: kinetic energy, the energy of a moving body, is abbreviated KE in physics
a ton is slang for a hundred miles an hour

explanation.surface: A performer full of lively energy who builds up to tremendous pace.
explanation.walkthrough: Kinetic energy is energy due to motion, written KE; doing a ton means driving at 100mph.
explanation.definitionFit: Buster Keaton was the great silent-film comic actor famed for his deadpan stunts.

clue.text: We want to know: who is the earth goddess?

definitions.meaning: a request for information: inform us
the Roman goddess of the earth, also called Terra Mater

explanation.surface: A curious crowd asking which deity rules the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words it is the demand 'tell us'; as one it is the Roman earth goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman deity personifying the earth bore this name, and split it is the plea for information.

clue.text: Copper briefly said au revoir

indicators.note: said means the letters are spoken out loud to give the entry

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, a short form of its Latin name

explanation.surface: A policeman curtly said goodbye in French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal; spoken, the letters C U make the farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Au revoir is French for goodbye until we meet again, the same as the casual English farewell.

clue.text: Start to rail with a very strong wind getting up under canvas: "Who fixed the holiday?"

indicators.note: under canvas means sheltered inside a tent, so the pieces go inside it

parts.note: a tent is made of canvas

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of the following word
in a down clue getting up means rising, so the word reads from the bottom

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind

explanation.surface: A camping holiday ruined by a storm, with the victim asking who booked it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting up' reverses the wind into ELAG, read upwards as this is a down clue; 'under canvas' is the container image, everything sheltering inside the tent.
explanation.definitionFit: A travel agent is the person or firm that arranges holidays for customers.

clue.text: Fabulous place giving superior Eurovision winner kiss on return

indicators.note: on return means the whole string of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: U stands for upper class, socially superior
Dana won the Eurovision Song Contest for Ireland in 1970
X is the conventional written sign for a kiss

explanation.surface: A dream venue where a song contest champion gets a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on return' reverses UDANAX. U as upper-class comes from the old U and non-U distinction.
explanation.definitionFit: Xanadu is the legendary pleasure-palace site in Coleridge's Kubla Khan, now any idyllic spot.

clue.text: Rubbish offered by stars in business clubs

parts.note: rot is nonsense or rubbish
Aries is a constellation, a group of stars, and a zodiac sign

explanation.surface: A dismissal of horoscopes in a businessmen's gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stars' hints at horoscopes, apt since Aries is a star sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotary Clubs are service organisations for business and professional people.

clue.text: Man who sketched nothing, a dim-witted chap

parts.note: Boz was the pen-name Dickens used for his early Sketches by Boz
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: An artist who drew a blank is called a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sketched' suggests a draughtsman, but it points to Dickens's Sketches by Boz.
explanation.definitionFit: A bozo is an informal word for a stupid or foolish man.

clue.text: What a country mad about the Co-op might have been? That's conjecture

parts.note: the divi was the dividend paid to Co-op members, something its shoppers were keen on
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: Imagining a whole land obsessed with collecting its grocery dividend.
explanation.walkthrough: The British Co-operative stores paid members a dividend, the divi; a country devoted to it would be a divi nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Divination is foretelling by intuition or omens, hence guesswork or conjecture.

clue.text: A medical god I use with scapula broken

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed up and put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A doctor deity explains how he treats a fractured shoulder blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges IUSE and SCAPULA, eleven letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesculapius was the Roman god of medicine and healing, son of Apollo.

clue.text: Cathedral cleaner, very appropriate for that area

parts.note: a char or charwoman is a cleaner
tres is French for very, fitting since the cathedral is in France

explanation.surface: A cleaner at a church who is just right for the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is an old British word for a cleaning woman. 'that area' is France, where the cathedral stands, so very is given in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartres is the French town whose Gothic cathedral is famed for stained glass.

clue.text: Chemical in river on isle — tons disposed of

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

indicators.note: disposed of means that letter is removed from the island's name

parts.note: the Isle of Thanet is in Kent

explanation.surface: A pollutant in a river on an island after tons are dumped.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a Yorkshire river and the Isle of Thanet is the north-east tip of Kent; 'disposed of' drops a T from THANET.
explanation.definitionFit: Urethane is an organic compound used in making plastics and formerly as an anaesthetic.

clue.text: In the role of a greedy person with clam to eat

parts.note: qua is Latin meaning in the capacity of
a hog is a greedy person

explanation.surface: A glutton gets a shellfish to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: The quahog is a hard-shelled edible clam of the North American Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Company that is full of conflict — not a Shell?

indicators.note: full of means the conflict piece goes inside the other letters

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

indicators.note: not a means the letter a is left out of the conflict word

parts.note: war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: A firm riven by infighting that is not the oil giant Shell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' leaves WR; the question mark and capital S tempt you towards the oil company, but this is a seashell.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowrie is a sea snail with a glossy shell, once used as money.

clue.text: So two heads of state spoke across the Atlantic? That's criminal!

parts.note: Bush was US President, the American head of state
rang means phoned, as on a transatlantic call
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the British Queen, head of state

explanation.surface: A president and a queen talking on the phone are up to no good.
explanation.walkthrough: The two heads of state are President Bush and the Queen, ER; one rang the other over the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A bushranger was an Australian outlaw living in the bush, so a criminal.

clue.text: Interjection of surprise about a right rude sign — made by him?

definitions.text: Interjection of surprise about a right rude sign — made by him?

indicators.note: about means the surprised exclamation wraps round the other letters

parts.note: hey is an exclamation of surprise
a V-sign is a rude gesture in Britain

explanation.surface: A gasp at an obscene gesture, and a guess at who made it.
explanation.walkthrough: The showjumper Harvey Smith famously gave judges a V-sign in 1971; in Britain a V-sign made with the palm inward is rude.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes the rider Harvey Smith, notorious for flashing a rude two-fingered sign.

clue.text: Please let's have a non-CFC deodorant!

definitions.meaning: an impatient wish for something to come soon
a deodorant applied by a rolling ball rather than an aerosol spray containing CFCs

explanation.surface: A plea for an ozone-friendly antiperspirant.
explanation.walkthrough: CFCs were gases in aerosol sprays, so a deodorant without them is applied by a rolling ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both an exclamation urging something to hurry up and a ball-applied deodorant.

clue.text: Old kingdom threatened with something like the boot, way back

definitions.text: Old kingdom threatened with something like the boot

indicators.note: back means the word for way is read in reverse

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner

explanation.surface: An ancient realm under threat from footwear, pushed back.
explanation.walkthrough: Psalm 60 says 'over Edom will I cast out my shoe', the threat of something like the boot.
explanation.definitionFit: Edom was an ancient kingdom south of the Dead Sea, cursed in the Bible.

clue.text: The female artist leading the fashion, following an earlier designer?

indicators.note: leading means these pieces come before the fashion word

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
the ton is fashionable society, from French bon ton

explanation.surface: A woman painter setting the trend, in the footsteps of a past designer.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, Royal Academician, is the stock crossword artist; 'the ton' is an old word for high fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Sheraton was an eighteenth-century English furniture designer.

clue.text: The French prostitute said to be in the capital

parts.note: la is the French word for the

indicators.note: said means the word for prostitute is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a whore is a prostitute

explanation.surface: A French streetwalker is reported to be in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: The silent W means the spoken word sounds like HORE; Lahore is a provincial capital, not a national one.
explanation.definitionFit: Lahore is the capital of Pakistan's Punjab province.

clue.text: Farmyard companion embraced by piggie

parts.note: a horse, another baby-talk farm animal; and the two letters G, G spelt out, held inside the word piggie

explanation.surface: A nursery picture of a pig hugging a fellow farm animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of PIGGIE holds two Gs; say each letter's name and you get the nursery word for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Gee-gee is the childish word for a horse, a natural farmyard companion.

clue.text: Jar? Its opening needs weight applied

definitions.text: Jar? Its opening needs weight applied

indicators.note: its opening means the first letter of the word jar

parts.note: an ounce is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Instructions for prising open a stuck jar lid with pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is both definition and recipe: the J of 'Jar' plus OUNCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To jounce is to jolt or bounce, and jar also means to jolt.
